title: Code challenges with input/output contracts
learningObjectives: Explain the concept and its relevant rules.
Trace the example and justify its behaviour.
Identify important assumptions and failure cases.
Apply the concept in a reviewed and tested exercise.

understand.concept: A code challenge defines an input format, output format, constraints, required behaviour and evaluation rules. A good solution respects the contract for all permitted inputs, not only the sample case.
understand.whyItMatters: Explicit contracts make challenges fair, testable and suitable for automated evaluation.
understand.analogy: Treat standards, interfaces and release steps as explicit contracts that make assumptions visible.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not replace the C standard, implementation documentation or project-specific requirements.

explain.narrative:
A code challenge defines an input format, output format, constraints, required behaviour and evaluation rules. A good solution respects the contract for all permitted inputs, not only the sample case.

State assumptions and constraints, consult the applicable standard or tool documentation, and verify the result with appropriate compiler diagnostics and tests. Separate portable guarantees from implementation-specific behaviour.

examples.title: Focused C example
examples.explanation: The example reads one integer, validates a simple constraint and prints the required result. A real challenge must state whether multiplication overflow is possible and how invalid input is handled.

practise.guidedTask: Write a complete input/output contract for a program that sums two integers.
practise.independentTask: Create three test cases including a boundary case and an invalid-input case. State which inputs are inside the challenge contract.
hints: Do not infer input constraints from sample values alone.
Use exact output formatting when an automated judge compares output.
Check arithmetic limits implied by the constraints.
